#### MGR-TELLER-005 — User-Employee UUID linkage, email uniqueness and atomic conflict handling

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER performing Teller create or update.
- **User objective:** Preserve single linked Employee identity and avoid overwriting another Employee or login.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** Within createOrUpdateTeller Core locks selected User UUID and resolves Employee by existing link then Employee unique email then creates new. Employee whose User is a different UUID rejected with 409; email reused by another Employee rejected; known DB Employee email uniqueness race translated into ConflictException while other data-integrity errors remain errors. Employee and User each reference same TELLER Role after successful transaction, Employee status ACTIVE, User.employee_id unique FK protects reuse. Employee.email is independent of User.email; User username/email also independently unique. Manager web surfaces definitive 409 and refreshes directory without automatically replaying POST/PUT. Transactional saveAndFlush Employee, save User and session revocation happen together, and User row lock serializes same-target mutations.
- **Frontend / Android:** [bank-web/components/banking/ManagerTellerDirectory.tsx](https://github.com/gimesha-adikari/bank-web/blob/012fbc6ff2687d126c67c85ce54cfc8d16f79f27/components/banking/ManagerTellerDirectory.tsx); [bank-web/lib/api/tellers.ts](https://github.com/gimesha-adikari/bank-web/blob/012fbc6ff2687d126c67c85ce54cfc8d16f79f27/lib/api/tellers.ts). #### MGR-TELLER-007 — Manager Teller profile editing with forced active-state synchronization

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER editing linked User/Employee.
- **User objective:** Maintain Teller employment profile without unintentionally changing login credentials.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** Select a row with linked User UUID, click Edit Teller profile, prefill Employee first/last/email/phone/address/gender/dateOfBirth/department; validate required fields, email/length, past DOB; submit PUT /api/v1/tellers/{User UUID} with TellerRequest through CSRF BFF. Controller MANAGER-only invokes transactional createOrUpdateTeller. Service changes Employee attributes and always sets Employee.role=TELLER, status=ACTIVE, resignationDate=null, and User.role=TELLER, without changing User.email, username or password; normal ACTIVE unchanged-role profile editing does not revoke sessions. If optional request.managerId supplied to Core, service looks up Employee manager by UUID and updates it; Manager UI never sends managerId and current manager remains. API returns 200 literal Teller updated, UI reloads directory. UI explicitly warns Employee email edits do not update User login email. 400/409/401/403 and uncertain errors handled separately.

#### MGR-TELLER-008 — INACTIVE Teller activation and conditional reattachment after removal

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER handling inactive or formerly removed Employee.
- **User objective:** Restore eligible Teller access while preserving prior employment identity where possible.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** Core Status enum ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PENDING, RESIGNED. When an INACTIVE Employee is still linked to User, Manager sees Reactivate and edit profile; PUT /tellers/{User UUID} invokes createOrUpdateTeller and forces Employee ACTIVE, User/Employee TELLER, resignationDate null, revoking sessions if status changed. But confirmed removal detaches User and keeps Employee INACTIVE with userId=null, so its former row has no Edit/Reactivate button. Manager may select now-CUSTOMER User under Assign Teller and POST; Core can reuse detached Employee by matching email, preserving UUID/hireDate if same; otherwise cannot guarantee original Employee reuse. There is no explicit /reactivate, restore by Employee UUID, status dropdown, suspend/RESIGNED/PENDING transition, new credential flow or row-specific reattachment UI. Admin separate generic status editor Part11.

#### MGR-TELLER-009 — Confirmed Teller removal, CUSTOMER demotion and retained former Employee

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER removing ACTIVE linked Teller.
- **User objective:** Remove Teller operating authority without deleting User or Employee history.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** Select ACTIVE linked row, click Remove Teller assignment, read confirmation of INACTIVE, User.role CUSTOMER, detached association, session revocation and 401/403. On Confirm issue CSRF DELETE /api/v1/tellers/{User UUID}; MANAGER-only Controller invokes @Transactional EmployeeServiceImpl.resignEmployee: lock User, load Employee by linked User UUID, reject missing/already inactive, set Employee.status INACTIVE and resignationDate now, save; find CUSTOMER role and set User.role CUSTOMER, User.employee=null, Employee.user=null; revoke all User sessions. Return HTTP 204; UI shows confirmation then reloads Teller+User lists. Employee.role TELLER and Employee row remain, so historical former Teller appears INACTIVE/null userId but no editing/removal controls. User/username/password, existing banking Customer/Account/history retained untouched. Repeat remove by former User UUID finds no Employee and is not safely idempotent.

#### MGR-TELLER-010 — Role and Employee eligibility enforcement with persisted session revocation

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER changes; existing CUSTOMER and TELLER users affected.
- **User objective:** Prevent old tokens from continuing Teller operations after role or Employee status changes.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** Promotion createOrUpdateTeller detects User role not TELLER, missing Employee or Employee not ACTIVE, and calls AuthService.revokeAllSessions(userId) after persisting. Removal always revokes. Core deletes stored session rows, and JwtAuthFilter checks JWT subject/role plus server-side Session fingerprint and current User.matchesAuthorization: User.isActive, not BANNED, current role matches token and linked Employee.status ACTIVE. Old CUSTOMER/TELLER bearer after promotion/demotion receives 401 even if signature valid, refresh cannot revive; a fresh login with existing username/password returns current role. Fresh CUSTOMER cannot access TELLER account POST (403). Pure unchanged ACTIVE Teller profile updates need not revoke; previously revoked token remains invalid after any later restoration. Browser AuthProvider handles expired 401; Android auth validates token but lacks staff-specific lifecycle UX. Generic AUTH session architecture retained Part01.

#### MGR-TELLER-011 — Read-only reconciliation after ambiguous Manager Teller mutations

- **Review part:** 09 — Manager Teller lifecycle.
- **User roles:** MANAGER after POST/PUT/DELETE unknown outcome.
- **User objective:** Avoid duplicate lifecycle writes and inspect current authoritative state following interrupted responses.
- **Workflow boundary:** Defined Manager lifecycle objective above; not a duplicate of AUTH-003/005/008 session internals, STAFF-CUST User/Customer creation, STAFF-ACC Teller account opening or reserved full Admin role management Part 11.
- **Complete workflow steps:** ManagerTellerDirectory writeInFlight ref and writePending disable double submit while request pending. On network, timeout, retryable transport or unclassified 5xx (including BFF 502/504), it does NOT resend mutation; calls reconcile(attempt) GET /tellers, plus GET /tellers/users for removals. Assignment comparison by User UUID and role TELLER/status ACTIVE; edit compares full profile and ACTIVE; removal requires Employee old email INACTIVE/null User UUID and User role CUSTOMER. Matching state displays previous response interrupted but confirmed by read-only refresh. Unmatched or failed reads preserve unresolved attempt, block new write and offer Check current state; advice to contact authorized Manager. Definitive 401/403/404/409/400/422/429 never automatically retry; 409 refreshes directory. On confirmed 201/200/204 but subsequent reload fails, success acknowledged with warning. No Idempotency-Key, persisted operation record/receipt, compare-and-swap or cross-page recovery; readback may reflect another Manager's change and cannot attribute actor. Reload loses local unresolved state.

## 12. Future implementation candidates

**Part 01 candidates based on traced auth implementation.** Ideas only; no work authorized. Do not implement these during review or treat an opportunity as a proven defect.

| Candidate | Related feature ID | Evidence for opportunity | Priority / decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native Android email-verification, resend and reset completion | AUTH-001, AUTH-002, AUTH-006 | Android AuthApi / screens lack verification/resend and reset-completion flows despite web support | Undecided |
| Align Android password-change reauthentication | AUTH-007, AUTH-011 | Core revokes all sessions on change while Android profile retains success state until a later 401 | Undecided |
| Standardize verified email-change link target | AUTH-009 | Email-change mail uses app.baseUrl; web result BFF expects its own origin | Undecided |
| Define intentional refresh/session-expiry experience | AUTH-004, AUTH-013 | Web blocks backend rotation; backend session expires at two hours and Android does not rotate | Undecided |
| Active-device/session listing and selective revocation | AUTH-005, AUTH-011 | Persisted sessions exist without user session-management UI/API | Undecided |
| Decide on secure multi-factor authentication separately from app lock | AUTH-012 | Android local PIN/biometric gate does not protect Spring API with MFA | Undecided |
| Assess distributed login-throttling operation | AUTH-016 | Limiter is in-process Caffeine buckets rather than shared across nodes | Undecided |
| Confirm per-channel username-change and recheck requirements | AUTH-014, AUTH-017 | Android change flow submits currentPassword but updateProfile does not evaluate it; web has no editor | Undecided |
| Core–FastAPI internal-identity lifecycle | AUTH-015 | Static shared secret authenticates KYC service requests without managed rotation workflow | Undecided |
| Implement customer correction/resubmission for NEEDS_MORE_INFO | KYC-008 | Controller returns active case before replacement; web has no correction form | Actual missing journey; undecided |
| Replace Android local placeholder liveness/face indicators | KYC-013 | Android assigns 0.9 on selfie without real check feedback | Partial native experience; undecided |
| Add Android rejected-case restart and error/retry recovery | KYC-013, KYC-014 | Web supports restart and idempotent reconciliation, Android does not | Missing cross-client steps; undecided |
| Validate actual FastAPI models/runtime and KYC end-to-end acceptance | KYC-004 | Default simple backends, advanced ONNX weights absent in reviewed GitHub, no run evidence | Evidence/assurance opportunity; undecided |
| Decide whether ADDRESS_MATCH and DOC_VALIDITY should gate approval | KYC-004 | Checks computed but policy decide() ignores them | Optional policy decision; undecided |
| Align 1 MiB/10 MiB/11 MiB upload limits and orphan retention | KYC-002, KYC-010 | Limits differ; retention only terminal referenced files | Operational design; undecided |
| Persist unfinished uploads and standardize submission idempotency | KYC-002, KYC-003, KYC-013 | Uploads persist separately, UI drafts volatile, Android no key | Partial workflow; undecided |
| Consider KYC case history and progress notifications | KYC-005 | Customer can query only latest case; web manual refresh | Optional enhancement; undecided |
| Clarify Spring KYC eligibility role rules | KYC-001 | Web CUSTOMER guard vs Spring authenticated-any-role KYC routes | Authorization product policy; undecided |
| Explicitly retain separate approved KYC -> Customer registration step | KYC-011 | Banking Customer not auto-created, additional fields mandatory | Product design; undecided |
| Define SUPERSEDED lifecycle and re-verification requirements | KYC-007 | Enum exists without known transition setter | Optional design; undecided |

| Unify web User and banking Customer profile presentation | DASH-005/006/007 | Web /profile reads User only; Customer editing is under onboarding and overlapping fields can diverge | Undecided |
| Expose supported User contact updates on web where desired | DASH-007 | PUT /users/me persists User contact information, but web lacks a general edit form | Undecided |
| Show more consistent KYC status and retry on dashboard | DASH-003/016 | Web queries KYC only for empty accounts; Android My Accounts treats unknown KYC as Start Verification | Undecided |
| Offer consolidated count/total or source-backed recent activity | DASH-002/009 | Web account cards contain stored balances but no total; Android Home activity is hardcoded | Undecided |

| Correct Android currency label and unavailable/loading indicators | DASH-008 | Home balance uses real account API but renders dollar sign and ignores HomeViewModel error/loading | Undecided |
| Reconcile Android User editing with email verification and authoritative reread | DASH-013, AUTH-009 | UI optimistically changes email although backend holds pending verification; blank fields can be ignored | Undecided |
| Scope Android default account by user if required | DASH-015 | Preference saved as device DataStore string rather than user-scoped server record | Undecided |
| Define whether broader customer settings/notifications are desirable | DASH-005/010 | No customer communication preferences, notification center or profile-photo flow found; no artificial L0 records | Undecided |

## 13. Known evidence limitations

- Part 00 inspected GitHub repository metadata, the default-branch refs, three known commits and root-level directories **only**.
- No frontend-to-backend workflow tracing, test inspection, API verification or live-stack acceptance was performed during Part 00.
- Matching the named local commits to GitHub main does not establish the absence of subsequent unpublished changes.
- No expected local commit was provided for bank-app, so local-vs-GitHub parity for the Android app is unknown.
- Future parts should provide source links pinned to inspected commits, distinguish documentation from independent verification, and disclose relevant access or version gaps.

- Part 01 inspected GitHub source only at the four pinned SHAs above, including web BFF, Spring security/services/entities, Android auth/storage/lock, and FastAPI internal authorization. No code was executed, no credentials tested, and no commits modified application sources.
- The committed Playwright tests run a mock core via `e2e/mock-bank-core.mjs`; they do not establish a real Spring/MySQL/Mailpit workflow. The Spring integration and unit tests were read as code, not executed in this review.
- No historical F1–F8 real-stack reports were found as readable evidence within the four GitHub trees. Their contents may exist outside these repositories; none were used to claim live verification.
- Android device/emulator runtime and email SMTP delivery were not observed. Hence all Part 01 evidence confidence is Source-confirmed and no Level 5 is asserted.
- Config-dependent email-change link destination and cross-platform difference in password-change sign-out are identified as completeness boundaries, not established live defects.
- Features not found in inspected source (MFA, social login, device-session management, etc.) are catalogued only as unsupported possibilities, not falsely scored as implemented.
- Part 02 inspected source only at pinned GitHub SHAs; no application source changed, and no tests, device/emulator runs, ML inference, real document processing, SMTP, or database mutations were performed.
- No attributable historical F1–F8 actual integrated-stack execution reports or verifiable outputs were accessible in the reviewed four GitHub repository trees; web Playwright uses mock bank-core.
- KycMlContractIT is environment-gated integration test source, not independently confirmed successful execution. Optional ONNX model weights are not tracked in reviewed bank-service source; local/external model snapshots were not available for verification.
- Part 02 found explicit source limitations in NEEDS_MORE_INFO customer correction, Android placeholder face/liveness indicators, mobile submission recovery and upload-draft persistence.
- Part 02 confirms latest approved KYC and separately saved Customer record are both required for self-service account opening; this review does not certify account-opening/ledger, Admin-workspace completeness, staff lifecycle or whole Android platform.

- Part 03 rechecked four GitHub main baselines and traced web dashboard, profile, BFF, Spring User/Customer/Account APIs and Android Home/Profile/My Accounts navigation and local settings. bank-service/FastAPI does not participate in dashboard or profile reads/updates.
- Web dashboard gets the Customer record for existence, account list for stored per-account status/balance and conditional latest KYC for no-account eligibility. It has no aggregated balance or real recent activity feed. Navigation links are not destination workflow verification.
- Web /customer/profile only reads User; banking Customer fields are maintained through /customer/onboarding with approved latest KYC. General backend User contact edits are available via Android, not a general web User editor; overlapping fields need not synchronize.
- Android Home uses real account-backed single balance but does not surface errors, uses dollar sign rather than LKR, shows fixed recent transactions and inert quick actions/Notifications; Android My Accounts and profile support real API reads/edits plus a device-local default account.
- Tests inspected but not run. Web Playwright uses mock bank-core; Android ApiContractTest covers serialization only; no attributable real integrated-stack Part 03 evidence accessible. Every Part 03 record Source-confirmed; no Level 5.
- Account lifecycle (04), transactions and ledger (05), Internal Pay (06), staff Customer management (07), and full Android app (14) remain not reviewed beyond Part 03 integration boundaries.

- Part 04 checked all four prior GitHub main refs at pinned commits, then source-reviewed bank-web, bank-core and bank-app account lifecycle. No Spring account-lifecycle call to bank-service/FastAPI exists, so no artificial FastAPI dependency.
- Core offers SAVINGS/CHECKING/FIXED_DEPOSIT with LKR opening minimums 1000/0/5000; Branch is persisted and required, but branch list ignores pagination, lacks status and branch admin mutations are stubs. No demonstrated interest/term/fee product lifecycle.
- Customer self-service POST /accounts enforces role, linked banking Customer and latest APPROVED KYC; Teller POST /accounts/{userUuid} uses a different role and bypasses latest KYC. Neither opening path checks Customer.status ACTIVE or account count.
- Self-service web opening holds page-memory Idempotency-Key and decimal string, Core persists user-scoped idempotency claim and account+ledger/funding under one transaction. Claims replay successful response; no-key direct API, Teller and Android lack this durable contract. Positive opening deposit posts from system vault to Customer liability; zero Checking does not post journal/transaction.
- Account UUID, 10-digit account number, User UUID, Customer UUID and integer Branch ID are distinct. AccountResponseDTO omits branch/currency/owner; customer /accounts/my lists all statuses and by-ID reads enforce ownership; staff /accounts directory has no pagination.
- Staff PUT changes type/branch (reuses opening DTO and ignores initialDeposit); staff-only DELETE checks ACTIVE and zero Account.balance and ledger-derived balance under a posting-compatible row lock, persists CLOSED and retains history. changeAccountStatus for FROZEN/ACTIVE exists only as service method without a route; no customer closure.
- Android opening has type and branch input but Double amount serialization, no Idempotency-Key/recovery and unwired KYC banner. Dashboard account display and My Accounts default choice remain Part 03; deeper ledger Part 05 and staff Part 08 and Android Part 14 remain NOT REVIEWED.
- Part 04 inspected existing mock-backed web Playwright, Vitest and Spring/Android test source without running tests; no attributable live real-stack acceptance was available; all confidence Source-confirmed, no Level 5.

- Part 05 reconfirmed unchanged four GitHub main commits and source-reviewed bank-web, bank-core and bank-app financial paths; no genuine bank-service/FastAPI dependency for banking transaction ledger. No source or database changes, no test execution.
- Web CUSTOMER deposit and withdrawal POST call Spring through CSRF-protected BFF with required idempotency keys; authenticated User-to-Customer Account owner, ACTIVE/LKR, ACTIVE liability ledger, active LKR system vault are independently validated. No external cash or payment settlement proven.
- PostingEngine balances debit/credit in immutable POSTED journals/postings, locks and refreshes customer Account rows in canonical order, prevents overdraft and writes Account.balance plus journal legs and mandatory legacy projection atomically. Transfer uses same infrastructure but whole Pay remains Part 06.
- Web financial amounts remain precise decimal strings, Spring rejects numeric JSON amount and uses BigDecimal up to 2 customer decimals/4 ledger decimals and LKR-only financial operations; Android history uses Double and misleading positive sign for withdrawal magnitude.
- Core financial Idempotency-Key for deposit/withdraw/transfer is required via requireKey, durable user/operation/key scoped claim with normalized fingerprint, cached POSTED journal receipt and original balance replay. Web same-key uncertain retry is in-memory only; no deposit/withdraw GET receipt lookup.
- Read-only reconciliation service compares stored account balance with journal-derived liability balance but no connected HTTP/scheduler/UI. Journal.status POSTED only, legacy Transaction has type but no status; generic transaction list/detail routes return placeholder text.
- Account-scoped customer/staff history is actual sorted legacy projection via GET /accounts/{uuid}/transactions, supports closed accounts and browser CSV; not a journal read API. Admin-only reversal API makes compensating immutable journal, but no connected Admin UI; complete review Part 12.
- Android deposit/withdraw payment UI is preview-only (no money moved); native per-account history is actual authenticated Core read distinct from hardcoded Home recent transactions. Full Android later Part 14.
- V2/V3/V4 ledger migration defines system vault/cutover assets, customer liabilities, balanced opening cutover journal and legacy history FK/precision; actual deployment outcomes not inspected.
- Web Playwright runs mock bank-core; Spring financial/MySQL integration and Android test source were inspected but not run. All 19 TXN records Source-confirmed; 0 L5. Part 06 onward remains NOT REVIEWED.

- Part 06 rechecked all four unchanged GitHub main HEADs and directly traced web Pay and alternate Transfer page, BFF, Spring transfer/receipt/idempotency/ledger/projection, and Android payment UI. The bank-service FastAPI ML repo has no evidenced Internal Pay financial dependency.
- Customer selects owned ACTIVE source (Account UUID), manually enters recipient Account UUID and LKR decimal-text amount, reviews exact fields and explicitly confirms; no recipient name/number lookup or saved beneficiaries, and payment KYC is not rechecked after opening.
- Web POST /transactions/transfer with required Idempotency-Key and CSRF-BFF invokes customer-only Core service, source owner and both ACTIVE LKR checks, canonical row locks, DEBIT source LIABILITY/CREDIT recipient LIABILITY; one POSTED journal, two postings and two legacy history rows with one idempotency claim commit atomically.
- Core internal TransferReceipt includes both resulting balances in persisted cached payload, whereas customer TransferResponse intentionally omits recipient resulting balance. Web verifies receipt identifiers, amount and currency before showing journal reference, payer result and posting time.
- Core GET /transactions/transfer/receipt is read-only, current User + TRANSFER + original-key scoped and returns only COMPLETED cached receipt; missing/PROCESSING maps 404 and is not proof of failure. User cannot query by journal UUID/reference in customer API.
- Web automatic postcommit timeout recovery sends GET, not repeat POST, preserving key/payload; if lookup is 404 or unavailable, UI remains uncertain, allows manual GET Check receipt or explicit same-key POST retry. Key and draft are lost after navigation/reload; recovery across sessions incomplete.
- Paid-in/pay-out movement visible as TRANSFER_OUT/TRANSFER_IN account-specific legacy projection, but public history has no journal/reference/receipt link, so historic receipt cannot be reopened. No connected external payment engine.
- Android Transfer/Payments route creates a UI-only draft, review and preview receipt, not a Core transfer; real Android account history can separately read transfer rows. Full Android remains Part 14.
- Existing Playwright mock Core tests, web API/money tests, Spring MockMvc/MySQL integration-test code were read but not run; no attributable live-stack F1–F8 acceptance proof found. All 15 PAY features are Source-confirmed, none L5. No application source changed, no financial operations or tests executed.

- Part 07 source-inspected role-gated staff Customers workspace, complete unpaginated Customer list and local seven-field filter, Customer detail, existing CUSTOMER-role User search, staff Customer create, Customer one-to-one association and uniqueness, personal edits, direct-API status mutation, Teller preselected-account link, Admin-only delete boundary and absent Android staff UI; bank-service FastAPI not in CRUD path. No source code or actual Customer changed.
- All staff roles ADMIN/MANAGER/TELLER GET /customers, GET /users/all (CUSTOMER role only), GET /customers/{Customer UUID}, POST /customers and PUT /customers. ADMIN alone DELETE /customers/{Customer UUID}; full Admin deletion deferred Part11. CUSTOMER user cannot use staff methods.
- Staff create starts from existing USER UUID with CUSTOMER-role web search, prepopulates name/email/address and requires Customer-specific details+status; Core resolves supplied User UUID and persists separate Customer UUID with FKs/unique User/email, but does not enforce target User role, activation, verification or KYC. No customer create key or reliable ambiguous-response recovery; duplicate uniqueness exceptions not explicitly mapped to 409 in create service.
- Customer.detail maps banking Customer identifiers/fields plus linked username/User UUID; staff PUT updates Customer name/contact/gender/DOB/status through User UUID lookup but UI freezes current status and identity, not User login fields. Status ACTIVE/INACTIVE/PENDING/RESIGNED has no connected edit/transition UI, and does not independently suspend sessions, accounts or postings.
- Teller Customer details link passes linked User UUID into staff account opening, but no Customer-specific accounts list/count/branch summary; actual staff opening Part08. Admin deletion existence, FK retention and secure confirmation observed only as boundary, not separately scored; full Part11.
- Web Playwright staff/customer tests use mock Core, Core customer deletion integration-test source read; no staff create/update real-stack acceptance run or independent F1–F8 attribution, all 10 STAFF-CUST records Source-confirmed with 0 L5. Android self-registration is not a staff Customer workflow. Parts 08–16 remain NOT REVIEWED.

- Part 08 directly inspected staff account web routes, BFF, Core Account Controller/AccountService/ledger, account entity/repository, customer/branch links, account history projection and relevant Android navigation and test source at the same four unchanged GitHub HEADs; no bank-service FastAPI dependency in staff opening. No application code/tests/data changed.
- ADMIN/MANAGER/TELLER have global unpaginated staff GET /accounts, GET /accounts/{UUID}, PUT metadata, DELETE close and GET /accounts/{UUID}/transactions. TELLER alone has POST /accounts/{target User UUID}; CUSTOMER only has self/open own and owner history. Staff Accounts directory has no search/filters/paging/owner/branch context; no branch scope.
- Teller form verifies linked Customer.userId handoff, fetches real Customers/Branches, displays distinct User/Customer/Account/Branch IDs and selects SAVINGS 1000, CHECKING 0 or FIXED_DEPOSIT 5000 LKR minimums; string decimal amount exact. Core Teller opening resolves User→Customer, does not require latest approved KYC or beneficiary Customer.status/role; positive deposit atomically posts vault debit and customer liability credit, zero Checking no journal. No external cash custody asserted.
- Teller POST does NOT accept or send opening Idempotency-Key and cannot replay or GET unknown result by operation; web ref lock prevents same-page double-clicks, and ambiguous 502/504/timeout switches to uncertainty with no retry action and manual reconciliation. Account receipt after 201 shows actual new Account number/UUID/balance/status and selected Customer/Branch context; GET-by-ID rereads status/balance but cannot verify owner/Branch because response omits them.
- Staff metadata review/PUT changes only type/Branch under Account lock, forwards existing balance in unused required initialDeposit field, does not move money; web preflight protects against obvious stale snapshots but no server CAS and no Branch readback. CLOSED metadata edits remain available. Status ACTIVE/FROZEN/CLOSED visible; no staff freeze/unfreeze/reopen endpoint/UI; refer ACC-013.
- Staff closure only ACTIVE exact zero, confirms and refreshes before DELETE; Core requires both stored Account and derived ledger balance zero under posting-compatible lock, responds 204 and retains CLOSED account/history; UI GETs confirmation and handles ambiguous DELETE by GET-only readback with no duplicate DELETE. Negative/nonzero or frozen blocked; ledger-mapping rules enforce independently.
- Staff history uses account-scoped GET actual persisted projected transactions newest first, empty/error/reload and client CSV; generic GET /transactions is literal stub, CUSTOMER-only financial POSTs do not enable Teller cash operations; full Admin reversals Part12.
- Existing web Playwright test source uses mocked Core, Vitest components mocked; Spring MockMvc/database integration tests source inspected for opening/closure/role/ledger/races but not executed; no attributable real-stack F1–F8 acceptance output, all 12 STAFF-ACC records Source-confirmed, no L5; Android has no staff Account area. Parts 09–16 NOT REVIEWED.

- Part 09 source-reviewed 11 Manager Teller lifecycle capabilities through unchanged four `main` commits; web Manager route/BFF, Core Teller Controller/EmployeeService/User/Employee/Role/Session, Android navigation and relevant test source. No direct FastAPI Teller dependency; no test execution, User/Employee or financial operations.
- MANAGER-only /staff/tellers and all /api/v1/tellers endpoints. GET Teller role Employee full directory including INACTIVE former rows and locally searchable fields; no paging, Branch/manager scope or Employee UUID in response. GET /tellers/users returns all Users, browser filters active CUSTOMER. Core POST restricts ADMIN targets only; cannot claim server-enforced CUSTOMER/active eligibility.
- POST Teller assignment uses existing User UUID, no new login/password/invitation/Branch, transactional separate Employee UUID creation/reuse, role TELLER on User and Employee, Employee ACTIVE, email uniqueness, session revocation and 201 text; fresh login with original credentials. User.email remains separate from editable Employee.email; ManagerId in backend only, not form.
- Inline Teller details expose Employee/User link and hire/status/manager ID but not Employee UUID/resignationDate/audit. PUT by linked User UUID edits Employee and also forces TELLER/ACTIVE; normal profile-only edit does not revoke. Still-linked INACTIVE can reactivate, detached removed Employee cannot from row; reassigning former User may reuse historical Employee by matching email.
- DELETE by User UUID requires Manager confirmation, sets Employee INACTIVE with resignation date, clears User/Employee link, changes User role CUSTOMER and revokes sessions, 204; retains User, historical Employee row and all Customer/account records. No idempotent repeat DELETE, status-specific suspension or direct rehire. JwtAuthFilter checks current role/Employee status and persisted Session, revoked bearer 401, fresh role token required.
- Client writeInFlight lock and read-only uncertain-result GETs avoid blind replay on timeout, but no durable idempotency/auditable operation receipt/cross-reload recovery; admin global User/Employee roles Part11, Android-wide Part14 and platform audit Part15 remain unreviewed.
- Playwright uses mock Core, Vitest mocked and Spring @SpringBootTest/MockMvc test sources inspected but not executed; all 11 MGR-TELLER records Source-confirmed, none L5, no independently attributable browser/Core/MySQL acceptance artifact. Parts 10–16 NOT REVIEWED.
